parts:
Hi Yifan,

On Ubuntu it is necessary to set an additional Rstudio environment variable.

Please try the following(this worked for me):
1). From a Linux shell prompt, type:
 %export RSTUDIO_WHICH_R=/usr/bin/R

2). Make sure that a link '/usr/bin/R' exists in your install and points to the following:
 /usr//lib64/RRO-3.2.2/R-3.2.2/lib/R/bin/R

3). Make sure that port 8787 is open on your system.

4). Open a web browser and point it to:
 http://:<your.machine.ip.address>:8787
This should open Rstudio with a login prompt.

5). If you want to permanently set the environment variable, 'RSTUDIO_WHICH_R' add it to your .bash_profile file in your user home directory.


Stephen Weller
Revolution R Open Technical Support

messages.author: 9ca0345d553844f2
messages.subject: Re: RRO-3.2.2 broke RStudio Server for me
parts:
As reported on Github, it may be related to the following: 

Line 4 in /usr/lib64/RRO-3.2.2/R-3.2.2/lib64/R/bin/R determines R_HOME_DIR based on readlink /proc/$$/fd/255. Since this command is implementation-dependent, it does not work the same way across each environment. Some users have had success by updating line 4 to use the absolute path to R such as: 
  • R_HOME_DIR=/usr/lib64/RRO-3.2.2/R-3.2.2/lib64/R 
  • R_HOME_DIR=/usr/lib64/RRO-3.2.2/R-3.2.2/lib/R

The actual path depends on your environment or distribution. Hope this helps.

Thanks,
Josée
